BRAND-NEW DEMO HERE
Developer Announcement
​
bio-Synthetica is a dark sci-fi adventure featuring turn-based combat inspired by the retro classics. Take on the role of R3-M1, a newly activated robot, as they venture through a dark, dystopian world in search of answers. Yet, the clues lie buried within dust and ash, data files and audio clips left behind by decaying corpses from a not-so-distant past.
However, in the shadows lurks an ancient evil—creatures stalking and hunting you at every turn. You must follow the breadcrumbs left behind by your creator in hopes of locating and protecting her. She gave you life, and you must save hers.
R3-M1 Combat Robot Model 1.0. Equipped with Mech-Blade and Particle Gun.
Buy yours today for just $5999!
​
Scavenge resources, discover schematics, and craft a variety of items.
Slower and more methodical combat requires a specific strategy for each encounter.
Exploit certain "reaction" states with various abilities for additional damage and effects.
New overkill system with a fatality-style finisher that's unique to each enemy.
No random encounters. All enemies are scripted into each map.
Find an ARENA-bot companion and upgrade them for additional abilities.
Fully voiced dialogue by a talented cast of actors.
Plenty of exploring, hidden rooms, puzzles, and combinations to decipher.
Dark and atmospheric with a horror/sci-fi theme.
NEW Overkill system!
Fill your overkill bar and slay your next enemy with a brutal fatality-style attack.
All surviving enemies have a chance to enter the Panic State.
Make love, not war!

posts.author: MemoriesLP
posts.body:
I played the demo and I loved so much the atmosphere, which was accomplished by having a really good art style and sound design. I could not even believe there was a combat in it because just walking around and interacting with stuff was making me interested in the game.
The idea of the protagonist being a robot with a tv face, that is walking on some post apocaliptic world or something, was really interesting, because there was a lot of personality of the protagonist. His animations are really cute, and he reacts with stuff using the tv screen, or his antenna, and you can really tell what the protagonist is saying.
The voice acting was also good, and so was the effect on the voices given each situation, like an audio file, or a ghost, etc.
Just this opening sequence really sets the mood, and made me interested in the game.
The combat also looks interesting. I see that each skill has real meaning to them, so I was using every single one of them depending on the situation. The row system is a good twist to the genre. It was not easy to survive, you have to make smart decisions.
With just the first 4 enemies I encountered, each one of them were unique in their own way and they were not just stat differences, they also had mechanics unique to each one of them.
The animation inside combat are also really nice.
If the combat keeps like that for the entire game, I can see it will be a really good expirience.
Gameplay loop also looks interesing. The upgrades look meaningful. I like how it looks like you keep looping back on previous areas with short cuts. It felt a bit rogue like dark souls, but I'm not too sure how to describe it yet. I say rogue like because I was constantly coming back to the "home base" and making myself stronger or unlocking new skills.
The pacing was also good! I would slowly learn stuff, but there was also some exploration to do. Some people could say this opening is too slow, because it takes a long time to get to combat. However, I feel like it was a good opening, because it was introducing me to the exploration mechanics, which looks like they will be important through the game.

Thank you so much for the feedback on my demo! Glad to hear you enjoyed it. I was a bit worried about my opening and having too much exploration. I know many players want to jump into combat, but I think that would really ruin the setting/mood of my game. Plus the entire chase scene with The Lurker wouldn't make sense if R3-M1 already had their battle upgrade. I'm still looking at this, though... because I have received some feedback that the opening is a bit too slow for their liking. Just trying to figure out how to add combat earlier, without ruining my dark/mysterious opening haha
I'm going to do a pretty big demo update in the coming week. Here's what I posted on my Discord and figured I'd share what you can expect for the demo (coming soon).
Also... bio-Synthetica will be available during Steam's June Next Fest 2023!!!
Spoiler:
Upcoming Update!
Full controller support!
This took time because I have special controls I had to get implemented to work with a controller (flashlight, behaviors, etc). Those are all implemented now.
NEW Communication Ring:
I completely revamped this. Instead of 7 keyboard keys displaying each behavior, you will now have a "communication ring" that will populate over R3-M1 to select their option.
Simplified Communication Module:
You will now have specific rings populate based on what type of question is being asked: "Yes" or "No" and then 4 emotions: Joy, Anger, Excitement, and Sadness (NEW).
Brightness Setting:
You can modify the brightness, so the game is playable on all systems/monitors.
Audio Rebalance:
I reduced the level of some music and sound effects, so they're less noisy.
Battle Lighting:
Added lighting to the battle maps!
Nano-mend Bundles
are now available to purchase at Sagrim's Emporium based on how many you have in your inventory. This will help lessen the grind of finding nano-mends when you're out.
More Quantum Crystals:
You now have 3 Quantum Crystal locations around the factory for faster travel back to the lab. None of these are hidden and are easily found and accessible.
Additional ROBO-Unit Options:
Repair & Save
- This will fully repair durability, refresh Repair Cells, respawn enemies, and save |
Save Only (NEW)
- Save Only with no repair, respawn, or refresh of repair cells. This option will allow players to save and not have enemies respawn. You can now take a break in the middle of your dungeon runs. |
Install Repair Cell
- No change HOLO-bot
NEW Settings Menu: You can now change game brightness, modify audio, turn subtitles/tutorials on/off mid-game, and more!
Training Simulator:
There is now a training simulator in the Laboratory instead of a battle tutorial on the first enemy. You can choose to train, repeat training, and I may add additional training down the road (picture below):
Also... here's a quick sneak peak at the new Communication Module and how it works:
Twitter Post & Video

posts.author: AeroFunk80
posts.body:
MONTHLY UPDATE: JULY, 2023
​
I'm excited to post a pretty big update this month. So, let's not waste anytime and get to the features and updates below:
Indie Detective Video Feature
bio-Synthetica was featured on the YouTube channel
Indie Detective
as "10 Indie Game Demos You Missed - Steam Next Fest 2023." You can catch the full video below (1:25):
Spoiler:
YouTube Video
Evasion Counter System
A new feature will be added to combat with the next demo update. Whenever R3-M1 evades an enemy's attack, a small slider mini-game will populate under you. If you hit the target quickly, you'll perform a counterattack and deal some additional damage to that monster!
​
Corrosion Build-up
In the current demo,
Corrosion
is a state that applies, and stacks, as a result of specific attacks. There are currently three levels of corrosion that do damage over time based on the level applied. This got irritating to manage and heal during combat. As a way to reduce the frustration, a new system will be implemented that will slowly build up with each corrosive attack or when R3-M1 performs a melee ability on dark bile enemies.
When the bar to the left fills up completely, R3-M1 will be inflicted with Corrosion Lvl 1. The bar then resets; if filled again, Corrosion Lvl 2 will apply. This will help players manage this debilitating state, giving them more strategy around avoiding it. Certain items will reduce build-up and remove the state altogether.
New Enemy & Battle Introduced Sooner
The biggest complaint I've received is how long it takes to reach combat. The beginning has a slow burn and takes a bit to build up, confusing many players about which type of game this is. Since bio-Synthetica is an adventure game and will feature a lot of combat, I wanted to find a way to introduce it sooner. Since you won't meet The Lurker and his minions until later, you will encounter the horrifying "Bile Rats" early on.
These dead rats have been infested and reanimated by the dark, mysterious bile that's been found around The Dilapidated Factory. They're weak and can be easily killed but possess a horrible attack that causes Corrosion build-up. Best to take them out as quickly as possible.
Mod System
In an attempt to enhance the player's experience of controlling a robot that can learn/upgrade its abilities, I'm adding a new mechanic that lets you equip three types of mods: Utility, Defensive, & Particle Gun. R3-M1 will receive various perks, benefits, and additional abilities when you find and install these mods. More details to come on this new system, including screenshots & videos. This will eventually be added to the demo with several mods to discover and install.
* * * * * * * * * *
​
I hope you enjoyed the update. Remember that the four new features above are not in the current demo. They are being implemented and will be featured in a demo update soon. Feel free to "watch" this post, wishlist my game on Steam, and follow to be informed once this update goes live. You can also join my socials located under my signature below. I'm very active with my community and willing to listen, adapt and implement popular feedback into my game. You can get involved in helping to develop bio-Synthetica, so comment, play, and leave feedback anytime!

You can read about all updates on my Steam page here:
Developer Announcement
I'd love any feedback you're willing to give. Feel free to stop back (if you try it out) and let me know what you think. I really strived to address many of my original demo complaints, so hopefully, this version will be a much more enjoyable experience.
NEW EVENT & ENEMY
Discover the new bile nest that transforms rat corpses into vile, dark creatures corrupted by the strange black substance found around the factory. Combat is introduced much sooner, as R3-M1 must eradicate these abominations. Destroy the nest to eliminate this new threat, or face these grotesque entities each time you enter a room with the infestation.
​
MODULATING R3-M1
A brand-new mod system has been introduced, allowing R3-M1 to further enhance itself throughout the adventure. Discover a variety of nodes and install them at the ROBO-Unit across three categories: Combat, Ranged, and Utility.
ARENA-BOT COMPANION
You no longer need to locate and repair R3-M1's ARENA-bot companion. Instead, discover the new Research Center and solve an intricate puzzle to release them. They will immediately join your party to assist in combat, eliminating the need to return to the laboratory for crafting and retrieval!
These are just a few of the demo's many new additions. My Steam page has more details!

posts.author: RCXGaming
posts.body:
Hello,
@AeroFunk80
! I always wanted to cover Bio-Synthetica because it looked extremely promising. The Feedback Festival helped push me to make this review, but trust me when I say I would have picked it out regardless due to the amount of work you put in to make the game look the way it does.
I got up to the Armored Brute fight and stopped after playing for an hour and 30 minutes.
--
Spoiler:
Bio-Synthetica Review
Spoiler:
Pros
+
This title screen is super sick looking with a cool soundtrack. Tells me everything I need to know about how spooky this game is gonna be.
+
The fact text appears when you hover over choices is pretty cool. Gives me some ideas, honestly.
+
All of this UI work is phenomenal, by the way. The ring menu for the main menu, the fact all the little usual RPG Maker menus slide in, the fact you give the player the choice to skip the tutorials, your little robot friend’s preview system, etc.
+
I’m really vibing with this apocalyptic future punk setting. Really speaks to my inner edgelord, especially with how there’s a ton of leftover apocalyptic logs – even voice files with actual voice acting. There’s a lot of effort put into this!
+
I love all of the little animations and flourishes the game has – your little character has a ton of adorable motion, and the little touches like stepping on a puddle and leaving behind wet footsteps is honestly kind of amazing. The game feels alive despite how dead the world is meant to be.
+
The little jumpscares are great. A corpse moving its head with a shock stinger SFX, etc. I do like that there wasn't anything truly obnoxious though, since the setting itself is already doing a lot of heavy lifting by being silently creepy. The rats in particular unnerved me the most because of the sounds they made.
+
A queueing system for the crafting is honestly kind of next level. I’d love to know how you accomplished this.
+
That little puzzle with the symbols was neat, as was the one where you have to do  a set of numbers in order.
+ (!!!)
There were no RTP sound effects throughout the entire thing!! You've legitimately done more than even a great deal of commercial RPG Maker games in that regard. Big applause all around.
+
I like how involved the cutscenes were, especially with our little robot buddy panicking and trying to open the door while the Lurker goes after him.
+
The battle system is pretty neat. I'm very fond of games that try to do the whole position awareness thing, as well as the checks in place to make sure you can't just spam your normal attack and expect to win.
+
That segment with the disembodied voices and the Lurker was genuinely quite chilling, especially with how you had to do number puzzles while he was chasing you – that’s a good setup-and-payoff for that mechanic! I also liked how he let up just long enough for you to run away.
+
The overkill skill and how there's multiple different animations upon using it on specific enemies is AWESOME. The fact it scares surrounding enemies is also a very cool idea - I wish more RPGs did this kind of thing. (EX. A lack of "He just ate Big Jim with a fork, you really think I'm just gonna stand here?!")
Spoiler:
Observations
=
Oh hey, it’s Olivia’s Horror Effects!
=
I do think it’s interesting whenever a game has like, social media buttons.
=
If I were to recommend a plugin for the title screen, it would be SRD’s Title Command Customizer and Title Choice Pictures, since it would remove the default RPG Maker menu from this set-up.
+/-
Interesting choice to not show enemy HP outright. I’m usually not a fan of this, but it is nice to see at least some visual feedback with the heart icon thing.
+/-
I also find it... fascinating that you made the detection of collectible objects an addon you have to equip instead of just something your character can do normally. Not a fan either, but at least it still exists even if you have to equip it.
=
I think it’s pretty hilarious that the battle entrance SFX is a jumpscare scream.
Spoiler:
Cons
-
No keyboard rebinding. Please install Yanfly Keyboard Config or have your coder create a custom version that fits your game. (And in your case specifically it’s kind of strange that you have this very custom options screen yet no rebind function.)
- (!!!)
The pace of the game is
extremely
slow. Every text box, step you make (you can't sprint) and combat action feels like it takes forever, and from what I could tell it was deliberate to preserve the mood or to make actions feel weighty. After a while, it genuinely gnawed at me - when I found a recipe to craft like, the Nanoheals or the Explosives, my reaction was more like "oh god I have to go back all the way or die just to make use of this."
- (!!)
Likewise, I find it very cheap how you can't really dodge the enemies due to how tight every corner was. And you can't sneak behind them either, given that they auto-detect you whenever you get close to them. Combine this with the fact you can't escape (which is odd because this is not the first game in this marathon to do this to me), and the "can we please get this over with" feeling really did start to build up.
- (!!)
The Armored Brute was where the mechanics kind of lost me. Combat was pretty easy/routine until this dude came along.
I tried everything - light attack, heavy attack, brutal double, push beam, etc. But it didn't seem to do anything, while he clobbered me doing the most damage out of any enemy in the game. The status tip didn't help either, since it just said "certain attacks will lift his shield state". I assume this means I had to learn the right skill or something, but if that's the case then I can see someone getting stuck on it for ages.
-
I think it's arbitrary to make the overkill skill also have an HP gate, since you already have to kill like, five enemies beforehand just to use it in the first place.
- (!!)
This is actually one of those games where I feel building it around action inputs would not only work tremendously, but also solve some of the jank. You and the enemies getting two hits randomly is cool, but whenever the odd "counterattack" prompt shows up I often beef it because it comes out of nowhere.
You use Light Attack a lot as is, as Heavy Attack leaves you open without much more benefit. So it'd make sense so the two-hit combo is actually part of the gameplay loop since if you miss, you just do the 1-hit version or whiff entirely. Given that you're ganged up by multiple enemies at a time and some of them can back up to avoid you, forcing you to use the pull beam or the particle blaster, I don't see it doing much harm anyway.
I feel it would make the game feel more exciting since it involves the player using their skill instead of relying on RNG.
-
Nitpick, but I felt the spookiness lift a bit when I started to see that the Lurker was the big bad guy. It was more effective when it was just a nebulous evil without a specific source.
Spoiler:
Overall Thoughts
Bio-Synthetica is one of the most impressive RPG Maker games I've ever seen - especially from someone who frequents our forum. It nails the atmosphere, has a very fascinating combat system, and is lovingly, grotesquely detailed with a ton of effort put into the little things. (And the big things too, like the
sound design!!!
)
It genuinely unnerved me at times too, which is a wonderful thing for a horror game of any stripe.
But where I feel the game falls flat is its pacing. The game is agonizingly slow, and due to this it stops feeling atmospheric after a while and mainly just becomes frustrating since you can't run, actions feel sluggish, text boxes linger for longer than they should and so on. The Armored Brute fight confused me more than anything else, and I didn't feel excited to jump back in to deal with it even though I was sitting on a big cache of scrap and recipes to better fight it with.
But man. If these flaws ever get ironed out, I can see this demanding a lot of attention once it hits store shelves. It has extremely high potential.
